title: Cleavage of the Fusion Protein (TEV Protease)
author: New England Biolabs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfd9ji96

steps.title: Concentrate fusion protein
steps.instruction: If the fusion protein concentration is below 0.5 mg/mL, concentrate it to a concentration of at least 0.5 mg/mL.

steps.title: Run pilot cleavage
steps.instruction: Perform a pilot TEV protease cleavage using a small portion of the fusion protein to assess cleavage conditions.

steps.title: Scale up and keep control
steps.instruction: Scale the pilot experiment linearly to the desired amount of fusion protein to be cleaved and retain a small aliquot of the uncut fusion protein as a negative control.

steps.title: Prepare cleavage reaction
steps.instruction: In a tube, combine 15 µg fusion protein with water to a total volume of 45 µL, add 5 µL 10× TEV Protease Reaction Buffer, then add 1 µL TEV protease, bringing the reaction volume to 50 µL.

steps.title: Prepare control reaction
steps.instruction: In a separate tube, combine 5 µg fusion protein, 5 µL 10× TEV Protease Reaction Buffer, and water to a final volume of 50 µL; do not add TEV protease.

steps.title: Incubate reactions
steps.instruction: Incubate both the cleavage reaction and the control at 30 °C for 1 hour, 3 hours, and 8 hours. Optionally, set up an additional reaction and incubate for 24 hours at 4 °C.

steps.title: Sample for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: At each time point (1 h, 3 h, 8 h), withdraw 10 µL from the reaction tubes and add 5 µL 3× SDS‑PAGE Sample Buffer. After the longest incubation (8 h or 24 h), also withdraw 10 µL from the control tube and add 5 µL 3× Sample Buffer.

steps.title: Heat SDS‑PAGE samples
steps.instruction: Heat the mixed SDS‑PAGE samples at 70 °C–100 °C for 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE analysis
steps.instruction: Load the heated samples onto an SDS‑PAGE gel and run electrophoresis to assess whether cleavage is complete.

steps.title: Remove His‑tagged proteins
steps.instruction: Because TEV protease and the cleaved MBP retain N‑terminal poly‑His tags, pass the cleavage reaction through nickel or cobalt affinity resin and collect the flow‑through, which contains the target protein free of His‑tagged contaminants.
